narrative.overview: This is an operator's tool, not a showcase: every screen exists so someone at Agência Coletivo can glance at a number, see if it's up or down, and decide the next move on a campaign. The system has two layers that deliberately look different from each other on purpose. The shell (login screen, admin panel) is the agency's own neutral territory — indigo accent, soft blue-grey background, no client branding visible until after login, because the point of that screen is that nobody should learn which clients exist just by looking at it. The dashboards (one per client) share one structural recipe — light cards, rounded corners, soft shadow, uppercase micro-labels, green/red/amber status language — but each is skinned in that client's own primary color, logo, and occasional named-category accent colors specific to their business. The two layers never swap vocabulary: the shell's indigo never appears inside a client dashboard, and a client's brand color never appears in the shell. The current recipe is deliberately plain (a souped-up spreadsheet), and that's an acknowledged, confirmed starting point rather than a fixed ceiling: the agency wants room to grow each client's dashboard beyond just an accent color into more of that client's actual brand identity over time, as long as it never compromises the fast-read KPI/table core.
keyCharacteristics: Two-layer system: a neutral agency shell + per-client-skinned dashboards, never mixing vocabularies.
One shared structural recipe (cards, radius, shadow, badges) reused across all 8 client dashboards, re-colored per client.
Status language (green = good, red = bad, amber/gold = neutral/attention) is constant across every dashboard regardless of client color.
Flat, light, high-density — built for a fast read and a decision, not for dwelling.

rules.name: The One Accent Per Client Rule
rules.body: Each dashboard has exactly one primary brand color, used for headers, active states, and primary actions.

rules.name: The Status Colors Are Sacred Rule
rules.body: Green/red/amber mean good/bad/watch everywhere in this system, independent of whatever client color is active.

rules.name: The Uppercase Label Rule
rules.body: Any field or metric name that isn't a card title is set uppercase, 11-12px, 700 weight, with slight letter-spacing.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Nothing lifts or deepens on hover. The only hover feedback is a color/background swap.

rules.name: The Two-Radius Rule
rules.body: A card radius and its children's radius are never the same number — inner elements always use the smaller step.

dos: Do keep the shell (login, admin) in its own neutral indigo territory — no client name, logo, or color should ever be visible before a successful login.
Do reuse the pill shape for anything meant to be scanned as a small status/category unit, and the two-step radius pattern for anything nested.
Do keep the green/red/amber status vocabulary literal and identical across every client dashboard.
Do treat the uppercase micro-label as the system's primary hierarchy tool at the component level.
Do look for ways to extend a client's brand identity beyond just the accent swatch as the system matures.
donts: Don't let a client's brand color leak into the shell, or the shell's indigo leak into a client dashboard.
Don't add hover elevation (shadow growth) to cards or tiles.
Don't repurpose a status color for anything other than good/bad/watch meaning.
Don't recolor the live-status indicator per client.
